question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 시간 부사구 'As a child'와 함께 과거의 역사적 사실을 서술하고 있으므로, 과거동사 'listened'를 쓴 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 선행사 'Santa Fe'를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이끌며, 뒤에 완전한 문장('he worked as a freelance artist')이 이어지므로 관계부사 'where'는 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어 'Houser's designs'가 뿌리를 '내려지게 된' 대상(수동적 의미 수식)이며, 'be rooted in(~에 뿌리를 두다)'의 수동태 표현의 일부이므로 과거분사 'rooted'는 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 뒤에 명사구 'his or her background'가 목적어로 오므로, '~에 상관없이'라는 의미의 전치사(구)인 'regardless of'는 올바르게 쓰였습니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 구조를 살펴보면, 'an attachment'는 앞 문장의 'a deep attachment to his ancestral background'를 동격 또는 부연 설명하는 명사구입니다. 이 명사구 뒤에서 수식하는 관계사절이 이어지는데, 관계사 뒤에 바로 주어가 빠진 동사구 'is shown in his artwork'가 뒤따르고 있습니다. 관계사 뒤의 절이 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장이므로, 이곳에는 관계부사 'where'가 올 수 없으며 주격을 나타내는 관계대명사가 필요합니다. 따라서 'where'를 'that'(또는 'which')으로 고쳐야 완전하고 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (B) 관계대명사 vs 관계부사 — 뒷문장의 주어 누락 여부로 판정
(C) 관계부사의 계속적 용법 — 선행사가 장소명사이고 주어, 동사, 목적어가 다 갖추어진 완전한 절을 연결함
(D) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 주어(Houser's designs)가 스스로 뿌리를 내리는 능동 주체가 아니라 전통에 깊이 박힌 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사가 적절함
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he __(A) listened__ to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment __(B) where__ is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(C) where__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(D) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, __(E) regardless of__ his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 of의 목적어로 올바르게 사용된 동명사 형태입니다. 주어인 '우리'가 '혼자 남겨지는 것'이므로 수동태 동명사인 being left의 형태가 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주어인 we가 고요함에 의해 '갑자기 사로잡히는(충격을 받는)' 수동의 관계이므로, 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 struck로 시작하는 분사구문이 오는 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 선행사 other people을 수식하며, 관계절 내에서 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사 who는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 형용사적 역할을 하는 과거분사 immersed를 지각동사의 목적격 보어 자리에서 수식하고 있으므로 부사인 similarly는 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: ⑤ (E) 'which' 뒤의 절인 'everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel'은 필수 구성 성분을 모두 갖춘 구조가 완전한 절입니다. 따라서 관계대명사인 which가 오면 격에 맞지 않아 비문이 됩니다. 선행사인 a reading group을 공간적 맥락의 부사적 의미로 연결할 수 있도록 전치사를 동반한 형태인 'in which' 또는 관계부사 'where'로 고쳐 써야 문장 구조상 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (E) 관계대명사 vs. 전치사+관계대명사 — 뒤에 오는 절이 완전한지 불완전한지 여부로 판정
(B) 분사구문 능동 vs. 수동 — 주절의 주어가 행동의 주체인지 대상인지 파악하여 판정
(D) 형용사 vs. 부사 — 수식하는 대상이 명사인지 분사(준동사)인지에 따라 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being__ left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly __(B) struck__ by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(C) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else __(D) similarly__ immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group __(E) which__ everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are something useful produced by a mind.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주어 자리에 'A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony'라는 두 개의 대상이 'and'로 연결되어 복수 형태를 취하고 있으므로, 복수 동사 'are'는 주어-동사의 수일치 상 완전히 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 대명사 'something'과 이를 수식하는 형용사 'useful' 뒤에서, '정신에 의해 만들어진 것'이라는 수동의 의미 관계를 형성하여 뒤에서 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 과거분사 'produced'는 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 형용사 'responsible'이 이끄는 형용사구가 선행하는 명사구 'the multiple overlapping technologies'를 뒤에서 수식하는 구조로 구성되어 있으므로 형용사 자리가 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 원급 비교 구문인 'as ~ as'의 첫 번째 'as' 뒤에서 명사구 'an invention'을 부사적으로 수식하여 '못지않은 발명품'의 의미를 구성하는 'as much'는 어법상 자연스럽습니다.

question.explanation: If 조건절 내의 구조를 살펴보면, 'a thousand lines of letters in UNIX'가 조건절의 주어입니다. 문장이 성립하기 위해서는 이 주어 뒤에 술어 동사(정동사)가 와야 하지만, qualifying은 준동사이므로 주어를 서술하는 정동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 이 문맥에서는 조건절 내부의 서술어가 필요하므로, 주어 'a thousand lines'를 단수 성격의 중량 단위나 전체 묶음으로 취급하여 원문의 'qualifies'를 쓰거나 수일치에 맞춰 정동사 형태로 고쳐 써야 합니다. 따라서 준동사인 qualifying은 잘못되었으며, 정동사인 qualifies로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (A) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 문장의 술어 동사 유무 판단
(B) 주어-동사 수일치 — 병렬된 두 명사 주어에 따른 수일치 판정
(C) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 수식받는 명사와의 의미상 태 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(A) qualifying__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, __(B) are__ in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(C) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(D) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is __(E) as much__ an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 선행사 a trait를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that절 안에서 과거의 사실('우리가 사바나에 살았을 때')을 서술하므로 과거시제 정동사인 kept를 쓴 것은 동사의 시제와 문장 구조상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 타동사구 write down의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 뒤이어 나오는 clauses에서 주어가 비어있는 불완전한 문장 구조를 취하고 있으므로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 전치사 by의 목적어로 동명사가 와야 하므로 동사 share의 동명사 형태인 sharing은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 비교급 행동을 병렬하여 인과를 나타내는 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문입니다. '더 많이 ~할수록, 더 많은 ~을 얻는다'는 의미에 어울리게 두 번째 비교급 앞에 the more가 올바르게 사용되었습니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장의 구조를 보면, 쉼표(,) 뒤에 주어가 생략된 명령문 형태의 주절인 'train yourself...'가 옵니다. 따라서 앞부분은 이 명령문을 수식하는 부사적 목적의 준동사구여야 합니다. 정동사 'Breaks'로 시작하게 되면 한 문장 안에 이렇다 할 연결어(접속사) 없이 두 개의 독립된 정동사구(Breaks..., train...)가 나란히 나열되어 어법상 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 부사적 용법의 'To break'로 고쳐야 '이러한 신경적 틀에서 벗어나기 위해서'라는 목적의 부사구가 완성되어 어법상 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (B) 준동사 vs 정동사 — 주절의 명령문(train)을 수식하는 부사구 자리이므로 준동사가 와야 함
(A) 정동사의 시제 — 과거 특정 동작이나 상태를 나타내므로 과거시제 서술어가 적절함
(C) 관계대명사 clauses — 선행사가 없고 뒷문장이 불완전하므로 명사절을 이끄는 what이 적절함
question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that __(A) kept__ us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). __(B) Breaks__ out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down __(C) what__ went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by __(D) sharing__ a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, __(E) the more__ reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 선행사 'shapes, colors, and concepts'를 수식하며 뒤에 'we have learned'의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 이어지므로 목적격 관계대명사 'that'은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 타동사 'recode'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 관계절 안에서 'see'의 목적어 역할을 하는 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 'what'은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구 'representing the world as abstract ideas and features'를 이끄는 동명사 'representing'은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어 핵인 'The discovery'에 연결되는 본동사가 필요한 자리이며, 과거 시제 동사 'undermined'가 술어 동사로 쓰였으므로 어법상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 주어인 'People'은 복수 명사이며, 수식어구인 관계사절 'who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail'의 수식을 받습니다. 따라서 이 문장의 진짜 주어 핵은 복수 명사인 'People'이므로, 이에 호응하는 술어 동사로 단수형인 'struggles'를 쓰는 것은 비문입니다. 복수 주어에 수일치되도록 복수형 동사인 'struggle'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 주어와 동사 사이에 길게 병렬로 이어진 관계사절이 주어의 핵을 가리고 있어 수일치 판단을 그르치기 쉬운 함정이 있습니다.
keyPoints: (C) 주어-동사 수일치 — 주어의 핵 'People'(복수)과 관계절 내부 동사들의 병렬 구조 뒤에 오는 본동사 수일치
(B) 관계대명사 what — 선행사가 없고 목적어가 비어 있는 불완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 기능
(E) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 주어 'The discovery'에 연결되는 본동사 자리 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts __(A) that__ we have learned through education. We recode __(B) what__ we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail __(C) struggles__ to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But __(D) representing__ the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely __(E) undermined__ the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 문장의 주어 자리에 쓰인 동명사구 'making time for exercise'를 이끄는 'making'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 전치사처럼 쓰인 'rather than' 뒤에서 동명사구의 형태인 'viewing'은 올바른 쓰임입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 시간의 부사절 'as you wait...'에서 주어 'you'에 상응하는 현재 시제의 정동사로 'wait'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구를 이끄는 준동사 'Incorporating'은 문장의 본동사인 'can improve' 앞에 위치하여 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: where 절의 주어는 전치사구 ‘of integrating mini-exercises into household chores’의 수식을 받는 명사구의 핵인 ‘the beauty’입니다. 명사구의 핵인 ‘the beauty’가 3인칭 단수이므로 이에 호응하는 동사도 단수형인 'comes'가 되어야 합니다. 복수 명사인 'chores'를 주어로 오인하여 복수 동사인 'come'을 쓰는 것은 문장 구조상 틀린 비문입니다. 따라서 복수 동사 'come'을 단수형인 'comes'로 고쳐야 합니다. 주변의 복수 명사들에 현혹되지 않고 문장의 주어 핵을 명확히 찾아내는 능력이 요구되는 문제입니다.
keyPoints: (B) 수일치 — 수식어구의 수식을 받는 주어 핵의 인칭과 수 판단
(A) to-v/v-ing — 문장 주어 자리에 명사 구실을 하는 동명사 판단
(C) to-v/v-ing — 비교 대상 또는 전치사 뒤의 동명사 목적어 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, __(A) making__ time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores __(B) come__ into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than __(C) viewing__ chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you __(D) wait__ for your morning kettle to boil. __(E) Incorporating__ quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: yet we hadn't noticed the sound during it was ongoing.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): that절 내의 주어 핵은 단수 명사인 a source이므로, 단수 동사 has는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어인 Your auditory areas가 예측을 수행하는 능동의 관계이므로, 과거진행형을 만드는 현재분사 predicting은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주절의 주어인 people이 '주장하면서' 경찰에 전화했다는 능동의 관계를 나타내므로, 분사구문의 현재분사 claiming은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): '~하곤 했다'라는 과거의 규칙적인 행동이나 상태를 나타내는 조동사 used to 뒤에 동사원형 run이 결합한 형태이므로 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 정답인 (B)가 포함된 문장의 부사절 구조를 보면, 주어(it)와 동사(was), 보어(ongoing)를 갖춘 완전한 절이 뒤따르고 있습니다. 전치사 during은 명사(구)를 목적어로 취하는 품사이므로, 절을 이끌어 부사절을 만드는 접속사 while로 고쳐야 합니다. 따라서 during을 원래의 접속사 while로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 의미상으로도 전치사 뒤에 절이 위치할 수 없음을 파악하는 것이 핵심입니다.
keyPoints: (B) 전치사 vs. 접속사 — 뒤에 절(S+V)이 올 때는 접속사 while을 써야 함
(A) 주어-동사 수일치 — 수식어를 제외한 실제 주어 핵(a source)의 단복수 판정
(D) 분사의 능동 vs. 수동 — 의미상 주어(people)와 분사의 능동 관계 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, __(A) has__ just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound __(B) during__ it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were __(C) predicting__ its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night __(D) claiming__ that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains __(E) used to run__ past their apartments.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 문장의 주어는 'The fast pace'로 단수 명사구이므로 단수 동사 'has'를 쓴 것은 수일치상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 전치사 to의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, doing의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 관계대명사 'what'은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 시간을 나타내는 접속사 as가 이끄는 부사절 내부에서 주어 'it'에 호응하는 정동사 'fills'는 주어와의 수일치와 시제 측면에서 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 접속사 when 뒤에 'it is'가 생략된 분사구문으로, 주어 'it(빨래하기)'이 수행되는 수동의 대상이므로 과거분사 'done'은 적절합니다.

question.explanation: no matter 뒤에 이어지는 양보 부사절에서 'it is'의 보어가 비어 있는 불완전한 격의 형태를 취하고 있습니다. 부사 how는 절 내부에서 형용사나 부사를 수식하거나 보어로 기능할 수 없으므로, 명사 역할을 대신하여 보어가 될 수 있는 복합관계대명사의 성격을 띤 'what'이 와야 합니다. 따라서 'how it is'를 'what it is'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (C) 관계사 vs 관계부사 — 뒤에 이르는 절의 명사 보어 자리가 비어 있으므로 명사 역할을 하는 what 필요
(B) 관계대명사 what — 전치사의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절과 불완전한 격의 뒤따르는 절을 유기적으로 연결
(E) 과거분사 vs 현재분사 — 주절의 주어가 '수행되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 done 선택
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle __(A) has__ us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to __(B) what__ you're doing at the moment no matter __(C) how it is__. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it __(D) fills__ the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when __(E) done__ with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수 명사인 a critical factor이므로, 단수 동사 determines를 사용하는 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 지각/인지 동사의 수동태 형태(be found) 뒤에서 주어(They)의 능동적 진행 상태를 묘사하는 주격보어로 현재분사 strolling을 쓰는 것은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 조건을 나타내는 부사절(If절)에서는 미래의 일이라 하더라도 현재시제가 미래시제를 대신하므로, survives라는 현재형 동사를 쓴 것은 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어는 단수인 One penguin's destiny이므로 이에 호응하는 단수 동사 alters를 사용하는 것은 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 구조를 분석해 보면 'The moment'는 'as soon as'와 마찬가지로 접속사 역할을 하여 시간을 나타내는 부사절을 이끕니다. 따라서 뒤에는 '주어 + 동사'를 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어져야 하며, '그 일(앞선 행동)이 일어나는 순간에'라는 의미를 형성해야 합니다. 이때 occurs는 자동사이므로 'that'은 관계부사(when)를 대신하거나 생략 가능한 접속사적인 역할을 하는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 which occurs는 어법상 비문이며, 원래대로 'that occurs'(혹은 'occurs'만 남겨두어 'The moment occurs')로 써야 부사절로서 완결된 문장을 만듭니다.
keyPoints: (C) 관계부사 vs 관계대명사 — 명사절/부사절을 이끄는 접속사적 역할의 판정
(B) 준동사(분사)의 태 — 주어의 능동적 행위를 나타내는 보어 역할의 분사 선택
(D) 시간과 조건의 부사절 — 미래 시제를 대신하는 현재 시제의 올바른 사용
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor that __(A) determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found __(B) strolling__ in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment __(C) which occurs__, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer __(D) survives__, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny __(E) alters__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time go by between oil changes, so to speak.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에 선행사인 'the distance'(단수)에 수치하는 현재완료 동사 has formed가 올바르게 연결되어 있습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 문장의 주어인 We가 바라는 주체이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사구문인 hoping을 쓰는 것이 적절합니다.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
